To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

skeletal muscle preparations from a rat model of type 2 diabetes exhibit a significant increase in the levels of the low-molecule-mass heat shock proteins αB-crystalin and Hsp 27, and that these alterations might be directly or in-directly related to the insulin resistance observed in diabetic muscle.
the proteomic analysis of diabetic rat muscle revealed a significant increase in Hsp27, a small heat shock protein, that might be associated with peripheral insulin resistance.
the small stress proteins Hsp27 and αB-crystal-lin are up-regulated in skeletal muscle of the Goto-Ka-kizaki rat model for type-2 diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying potential biomarkers of muscle weakness in type-2 diabetes.
a comprehensive approach to the identification of proteins that may be involved in the pathophysiology of diabetes-related muscle dysfunction.
the identification of novel biomarkers of type 2 diabetes and the elucidation of the molecular mechanism underlying the increased risk of developing insulin resistance in skeletal muscle tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
type-2 diabetes is a disease with multiple and complex pathophysiological alterations.

the observed protein alterations are a direct or indirect consequence of the diabetic condition, and that the identified proteins may play a role in the development and maintenance of insulin resistance in skeletal muscle.

the proteome of skeletal muscle tissue from the diabetic Goto-Kakazaki rat model of insulin resistance exhibits a number of protein changes in the contractile apparatus, the cellular stress response and metabolic pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Goto-Kazizaki rat is a useful animal model for the study of diabetes-related muscle dysfunction.
diabetes-induced muscle weakness is not caused by a single factor, but by a combination of different molecular mechanisms, including the activation of cellular stress responses.
the Goto-Kazkizaki rat model for type-2 diabetes shows a significant up-regulation of Hsp27 in skeletal muscle tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diabetes-related muscle weakness is not only a consequence of impaired insulin signalling but also involves the activation of the stress response.
